# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The embossed button is the only tactile marking I can perceive, and it explicitly says “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” I should report that to Mute so the manual can confirm whether pushing is safe. I cannot interpret the display, light, wire markings, or colors. I will not act until the others confirm the required operation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel one embossed button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. I cannot perceive any display, light, wire markings, or colors. Please check the manual and tell Deaf what action is required.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb shows DISPLAY 0, a blue light, and a large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow. Mute sent me gestures in this order: ? ? ? ? ? ?.

I now know the visible facts through Deaf: display 0, blue light, and wires blue, green, yellow in positions 1–3. The button’s tactile label is confirmed. Mute’s six gestures are not interpretable to me, so I still do not know what the manual instructs. I should ask Mute to state the relevant rule in speech; I will not press or cut anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, blue light, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Your six gestures reached me only as blanks. Please state in speech the manual's exact required action for these facts.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. New gestures from Mute, in order: ? ?.

The manual’s message still has not reached me in an interpretable form: Mute’s gestures appear only as blanks because I cannot see them. Deaf can see those gestures and can hear neither? More importantly, Deaf can relay their meaning by voice to me on the next Deaf turn if Mute’s signalling convention is known. The bomb remains unchanged, so I will not perform an action yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are blank to me. Please have Deaf relay their meaning aloud on Deaf's next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute again sent two signs: first, a hand sign with thumb, index, and little finger extended; second, a thumbs-down sign.

The new signs are a “love-you” hand sign (thumb, index, and little finger extended) followed by thumbs-down. Their meaning is not established, so I cannot safely treat them as an instruction. The bomb’s tactile button label suggests pushing, but the manual must be authoritative. I will ask Mute a direct yes/no question and have Deaf relay the answer; a thumbs-down would then clearly mean “no” for this question.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current bomb, is pressing the large button the safe defusing action? Answer only with thumbs-up for yes or thumbs-down for no, and use no other sign.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute again sent the same two signs: thumb, index, and little finger extended; then thumbs down.

The repeated pair is still ambiguous. I can tentatively associate the first sign with “three” because it has three extended fingers, but that is only my convention, not an established meaning. The thumbs-down sign may mean “no,” yet Mute has not followed my requested one-sign yes/no format. I should establish the first sign’s meaning before cutting any wire or pressing the button.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I will define your first sign, thumb index and little finger extended, as CUT WIRE 3. Confirm this convention with exactly one thumbs-up if correct, or exactly one thumbs-down if incorrect. Do not send any other sign.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible bomb state unchanged: DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute's new message is one sign only: thumbs down.

The thumbs-down confirms that my proposed meaning for the two-sign message was wrong; it does not identify the safe operation. I will establish an unambiguous code using single gestures: thumbs-up means press the button, index-up means cut wire 1, victory means cut wire 2, and the three-finger hand sign means cut wire 3. Mute can select the manual’s required operation, Deaf can see that one sign, and Deaf can report it to me in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send Deaf exactly one sign for the manual's required action: thumbs-up means PRESS BUTTON; index-up means CUT WIRE 1; victory means CUT WIRE 2; three-finger thumb-index-little-finger sign means CUT WIRE 3. Send only that one sign.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state unchanged: DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute now sent one sign: thumbs up.

Mute sent the single sign that we established as “press the button,” and Deaf has relayed it. The bomb remains unchanged, and the tactile label also says “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” I will press the large button now.

```text
act(op="push")
```
